facts.statement: The genus name Ticinosuchus means "Ticino crocodile" because it was discovered in the Swiss canton of Ticino.
facts.quote: The genus name means "Ticino crocodile" due to its origin from the Swiss canton Ticino.

facts.statement: Ticinosuchus lived during the Middle Triassic (Anisian to Ladinian stages) in Switzerland and Italy.
facts.quote: Ticinosuchus is an extinct genus of suchian archosaur (distantly related to modern crocodilians) from the Middle Triassic (Anisian–Ladinian) of Switzerland and Italy.

facts.statement: Ticinosuchus was a medium-sized, 2.5-meter-long quadrupedal carnivore covered in osteoderms.
facts.quote: It was a medium-sized (2.5 m long), quadrupedal carnivore covered in osteoderms.

facts.statement: The presence of sharp and recurved teeth indicates that Ticinosuchus had a carnivorous diet.
facts.quote: sharp and recurved teeth indicating a carnivorous diet

facts.statement: Anatomical features shared with other archosaurs indicate that Ticinosuchus moved with a fully erect, quadrupedal gait.
facts.quote: Key aspects of its anatomy that are shared with other archosaur relatives indicated a fully erect, quadrupedal gait.

facts.statement: A specialized calcaneus and ankle joint likely made Ticinosuchus a fast runner, unlike many primitive reptiles.
facts.quote: Esto junto al desarrollo de un calcáneo y una articulación del tobillo especializada, eso habría hecho de Ticinosuchus un rápido corredor, a diferencia de muchos reptiles primitivos.

facts.statement: Ticinosuchus is classified within the family Prestosuchidae.
The genus Ticinosuchus was described by Krebs in 1965.
The only known species of Ticinosuchus is Ticinosuchus ferox.
Ticinosuchus was a powerful crocodile-like carnivore with a shell of small bony plates covering its body, including its tail.
facts.quote: Este poderoso carnívoro, semejante a un cocodrilo, tenía una coraza con pequeñas placas óseas, incluyendo su cola.

facts.statement: Ticinosuchus measured approximately 3 meters in length.
facts.quote: Ticinosuchus medía cerca de 3 metros de largo

facts.statement: Ticinosuchus is one of the few terrestrial animals found in the Besano Formation, a site famous for its marine fossils.
facts.quote: It is one of the only terrestrial animals found in the Besano Formation, a fossil-rich lagerstätte on Monte San Giorgio renowned for its marine fauna

rejected.statement: The middle tail vertebrae of Ticinosuchus had an extra bony projection in front of their neural spines, a feature shared with only a few relatives like Rauisuchus and Batrachotomus.
rejected.quote: The middle caudal vertebrae possessed an extra, bony projection in front of their neural spines, likely for extra ligamentous attachments, an anatomical feature shared with a select few relatives like Rauisuchus and Batrachotomus.
